speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To understand the full picture, have you experienced any unintentional weight loss, fever, or changes in bowel habits recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age, nulliparity, and the rapid increase in abdominal girth causing shortness of breath, I need to determine if this mass is causing pressure on your diaphragm or if there is any sign of torsion. Have you experienced any sudden, severe abdominal pain, or has the mass been visible or palpable as a bulge before this recent rapid expansion?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Cancer with malignant ascites and diaphragmatic compression.

The previous suggestion of pyelonephritis does not fit your presentation of a large ovarian mass, rapid abdominal expansion, and shortness of breath without fever. To confirm the nature of the mass and the extent of the fluid accumulation, I am requesting an ultrasound of your pelvis and abdomen. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Abdominal_Ultrasound; REQUEST IMAGES.
